text.p: French proxy-vote holder Franklin Global Investor Services (FGIS) said on Monday that a shareholder owning around 38 million shares has instructed it to vote for a debt restructuring plan proposed by Eurotunnel SA/Plc.

"Franklin Global Investor Services received voting instructions from a shareholder owning approximately 38 million shares to change its voting position and vote for the restructuring presented to shareholders at the meeting (on) July 10," FGIS said in a statement.
Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle identified the investor last week in a French newspaper interview as Northern Cross Investment, a U.S. fund manager.
FGIS head Sophie L'Helias told Reuters the 38 million shares represents around three percent of Eurotunnel's capital. The decision reverses the investor's earlier opposition to the plan.
Lawyer L'Helias said the investor's decision to support the restructuring plan followed a meeting in Boston last week with Ponsolle.
"The necessary measures will be taken for the investor to vote its proxy," the FGIS statement said.
Other investors represented by FGIS were still opposed to the plan and would vote against the restructuring unless conditions previously stated were met, L'Helias said.
These investors' demands included a write off of 25 percent of the debt and a cancellation of the "substitution clause" which allows the banks to take control of the Channel Tunnel.
"This shows that a professional and rational investor who studies the plan can only conclude this is the best possible solution," a Eurotunnel spokeswoman said.

A spokeswoman for the French finance ministry earlier declined to comment on a Financial Times report that the French and British governments want a share in Eurotunnel's future profits in exchange for extending its licence beyond 2052.
"We are not commenting," said the spokeswoman who would only say that "the file is (effectively) being studied".
Ponsolle has warned Eurotunnel would go into bankruptcy if the restructuring were not approved.
